Sports.title: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in talks to sell stakes in Chelsea in deal that would value club at over £5bn
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in talks to sell stakes in Chelsea in deal that would value club at over £5bn

Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are in talks to sell their Chelsea shares to majority owners Clearlake Capital, talkSPORT understands.

Discussions, first reported by The Financial Times, have been ongoing for some time and are driven by a lack of strategic alignment, according to sources spoken to by talkSPORT. It is believed Boehly and Walter's market enterprise value of Chelsea is north of £5billion.



4 Boehly replaced Roman Abramovich as Chelsea owner after the latter's assets were frozen when Russia invaded Ukraine Credit: Getty

Boehly's vision centres heavily on creating success at Chelsea, generating football and brand value and maximising fan engagement. The appeal of the purchase was also in having an elite club in London.

Clearlake naturally share many of these values, but they are also multi-club focused with Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg important as both a standalone club and within the wider philosophy of how BlueCo works.

Boehly is set to step down as Chelsea chair at the end of this season as part of a pre-agreed plan when the consortium bought the club for £2.3bn in May 2022.



He was asked at the time by the consortium to become chair, with Clearlake getting to select the next one five years later.

Next summer has always been viewed as a potential parting of ways with Boehly hinting last year he could leave the club.



"We have to think long-term about what we're trying to accomplish," Boehly said in an interview with Bloomberg. "We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out.

"That's going to be where we're either aligned or we ultimately decide to go different ways."



All parties would ideally like to build a new stadium at Earl's Court, but the Earls Court Development Company are proceeding with their own development plans which don't include a football stadium.

With funding and permissions ongoing on that front, Chelsea must explore other options, including building on the Stamford Bridge site, renovating the existing stadium or finding a new site.

Those close to Boehly are less focused on where a new stadium is and more interested in how it benefits Chelsea as both a club and brand, and whether it would result in increased income on both matchdays and non-matchdays.

4 Boehly and Behdad Eghbali have had disagreements in the past Credit: Getty



The usage of the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has hosted NFL games, is viewed as a model to replicate by both Boehly and Walter.

Clearlake-Boehly paid around £2.3bn to acquire Chelsea from Roman Abamovich in 2022, who was forced to sell due to sanctions imposed when Russia invaded Ukraine.

Tensions between Boehly and Clearlake's Behdad Eghbali first became apparent in summer 2024 despite being denied at the time.

Boehly and Clearlake relationship

Eghbali has always been hands-on, including in recruitment, while Boehly felt frozen out of key calls and questioned the transfer model.



Clearlake sources at the time stressed billing the fallout as a 'civil war' was unfair, adding Boehly had a veto over all key decisions.

Boehly was believed to be against sacking Mauricio Pochettino, but did not use his veto at the time.

4 Many Chelsea fans will be happy with this news who have wanted Boehly gone for a while Credit: Getty

In 2024, Boehly was willing to raise funds to buy out Clearlake's 61.5 per cent stake in the club and valued Chelsea around £4.5bn.



Clearlake sources stressed at the time there was never any intent to sell, and this remains their position. They will either remain as majority owner with the current status quo or consider adding to their stake for the right offer.

talkSPORT understands Boehly and Walter now value the club at closer to £5bn.

Although an agreement has not been reached yet, and the idea of Boehly and Walter leaving has been on-off for some time, negotiations now have added urgency. Walter is seeking to sell assets with US prosecutors looking into his high-profile insurance companies.

Walter has already agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers for $12.5bn to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner, with the latter one of the key investors in Gianni Infantino's failed FIFA Forward Enterprise plans.



Chelsea, Clearlake and representatives for Boehly and Walter declined to comment when approached.

Sports.title: Former ball boy to land huge windfall as Au Vodka brand ‘strikes £500m sale agreement’
Sports.content:
Former ball boy to land huge windfall as Au Vodka brand ‘strikes £500m sale agreement’

A former foe of Eden Hazard is set to give his bank balance an almighty boost.

Charlie Morgan, the infamous ball boy Hazard kicked during a League Cup match in 2013 between Swansea City and Chelsea, is nearing a deal to sell his drinks company, Au Vodka.

2 Hazard received a red card for kicking Morgan Credit: Getty

Morgan is in discussions to sell Au Vodka to American beverage brand Sazerac Company.

How much does Charlie Morgan stand to make from Au Vodka sale?

The sale of Au Vodka is worth approximately £500million, with Morgan and co-founder Jackson Quinn to net £100m each from the deal.

Sazerac owns alcoholic brands like BuzzBallz, Southern Comfort and Fireball.

And Au Vodka, founded by Morgan in 2015, now looks poised to join them under the Sazerac umbrella.

Au Vodka's impending sale comes a year after Morgan told BBC Wales he intended to expand his drinks brand into the American market.

"If you asked a 25-year-old target market consumer in America, would they know Au? Probably not yet," Morgan said.

"So there's still so many more people who don't know about us.

"And I think we're still driven to try and take over the world a little bit more."

Who has endorsed Au Vodka in the past?

Au Vodka is widely known for its gold-coloured bottles and cans, with several celebrities endorsing the beverage.

Football legend Ronaldinho and boxing superstar Floyd Mayweather have both happily posed alongside Au Vodka products.

2 Mayweather had little hesitation in showing himself off with some Au Vodka bottles Credit: Instagram/@AuVodka

YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul even went as far as getting a tattoo of an Au Vodka bottle, although there was plenty of conjecture as to whether it was a real piece of body art.

Meanwhile, two-time darts world champion Luke Littler was another who has been a beneficiary of Au Vodka's generosity.

Upon turning 18 in January 2025, Littler was gifted a three-little Au Vodka bottle.

On the bottle was an image of Littler lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy shortly after his maiden World Darts Championship triumph.

That wasn't the only show-stopping gift headed Littler's way from Morgan's company.

Littler also received a giant gold dart which featured his nickname, 'The Nuke', on the flight.

Sports.title: Premier League club told to re-hire Steve Bruce as sack prediction made
Sports.content:
Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic has been tipped to be the first Premier League boss to be sacked this season.

And as a replacement, the Tigers will have a few options: Kieran McKenna, Scott Parker and even Steve Bruce.

3 Jakirovic has been tipped to be the first manager sacked in the Premier League this season Credit: Getty

Hull achieved promotion back to the Premier League for the first time since 2017 last term by winning the Championship Play-Off Final against Middlesbrough at Wembley.

Jakirovic was tasked with keeping the club in the second tier, but he incredibly ended up leading them to the top flight.

They are heavily predicted to be relegated this season though, and if they do struggle as expected, the Serbian could be sacked.

At least that's what former Premier League striker Troy Deeney thinks, as he tipped Jakirovic to be an early departure.

"I feel the Hull manager may go," Deeney stated on talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast when predicting which manager will be sacked first this campaign.

"If in the first month they're not doing well and the window's closed, he's the only one that can get changed, right?"

Who could potentially replace Jakirovic?

Should Deeney's prediction of Jakirovic's sacking come true, Hull will then have to bring a new boss into the dugout.

And host Sam Matterface began: "There are a few managers doing the rounds that could step into the breach..."

He went on to mention McKenna, who left Ipswich earlier this summer, and former Burnley boss Parker.

But Alex Crook bravely asked: "Get Steve Bruce back there?"

3 Bruce (right) spent four years as Hull manager from 2012, achieving two promotions Credit: Getty

Bruce was Hull manager for four years from 2012 through to 2016, taking charge of 201 games across his tenure.

He won 85 of those matches, winning promotion to the Premier League twice and leading the Tigers to the FA Cup final in 2014, which in turn secured a spot in a European competition for the first time in the club's history the following season.

The 65-year-old, who is a regular on talkSPORT, hasn't had a job since October 2025, when he was sacked by Blackpool.

What other Premier League managers are at risk of an early sacking?

Jakirovic wasn't the only sacking prediction made on the Premier League All Access podcast, as another name popped up.

New Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa is also at risk of being the first let go by their club this year, according to Matterface and Crook.

Matterface explained: "He's a rookie manager, he's following a man who built something that absolutely worked.

3 Arbeloa has also been mentioned as a potential first sacking of the season Credit: Getty

"They've sold their goals, there's no goals in that team. I just can't see it working out for him."

Pierre Sage was also mentioned by Deeney as another potential manager who could face an early sacking this season.

Sage recently took over from Oliver Glasner at Crystal Palace.

The 2026/27 Premier League campaign gets started on Friday, with champions Arsenal facing Coventry, live on talkSPORT.

Commentary from the Emirates will be coming from Jim Proudfoot and former Palace manager Alan Pardew.

Sports.title: Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe tipped to be beaten to Ballon d’Or by Champions League winner
Sports.content:
Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe tipped to be beaten to Ballon d’Or by Champions League winner

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has been tipped to be this year's surprise Ballon d'Or winner, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

Kane and Mbappe are among the frontrunners to claim football's biggest individual prize after the pair enjoyed stunning years for both club and country respectively.



5 Kvaratskhelia is arguably the best winger in world football right now Credit: Getty

After a record-breaking 61-goal campaign for Bayern Munich, Kane backed up his claim for the prestigious award by firing in six goals for England at this summer's World Cup.

But he faces stiff competition here, with France megastar Mbappe joined in the running by World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.

With the competition having a major bearing on the Ballon d'Or in recent years, Kane's England teammate Jude Bellingham and football icon Lionel Messi have also entered the fold off the back of standout summers, battling it out for the Golden Boot.



Kvaradona for the win?

With World Cup stars dominating the Ballon d'Or conversation, European football expert Andy Brassell has instead pointed to a player who played no part in North America this summer.

He called Paris Saint-Germain forward Kvaratskhelia a real contender for the award, pointing to his stunning campaign at club level.



The Georgian played a major role as PSG clinched back-to-back Champions League crowns in May, by beating Arsenal in the final.

Kvaratskhelia registered 17 goal contributions in 16 European games last term, which saw him named the 2025/26 Champions League Player of the Season for the first time in his career.



And Brassell believes his stunning performances in club football's biggest competition place him among the world's very best.

Discussing Kvaratskhelia on the Trans Euro Express, Brassell said: "If not the best in the world, really close

"I think to have that amount of ability on the ball, to bring it to bear usefully for the team and to do as much as he does without the ball, what more could you want from a football player?

5 Kane is a contender for the Ballon d'Or after a stunning season for club and country Credit: Getty



5 Kvaratskhelia showcased all of his world class ability in PSG's recent Super Cup win Credit: Getty

"He's got it all, and he's still only 25."

Brassell then tipped Kvaratskhelia as a major Ballon d'Or candidate, insisting his chances have been boosted after other favourites failed to take their chance this summer.

Victory in either of club or international football's biggest tournaments can be decisive in securing the individual award.

But with the likes of Kane, Mbappe, Messi and Bellingham missing out on World Cup glory, Brassell believes the conversation then moves back to the Champions League, where Kvaratskhelia reigned supreme.



He continued: "In terms of the Ballon d'Or, there's a chance because none of the players who could have made it theirs did.

"If Argentina win the World Cup final, Messi wins it. If England win it, then either (Harry) Kane or maybe (Jude) Bellingham win it.

5 Mbappe clinched the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot by firing in ten goals Credit: Getty

“If France win it, then Mbappe's got a case, and maybe a little side chance of Michael Olise. But none of those things came to pass.



"So eyes go back to the Champions League, and who was the best player in the Champions League last season?"

'He's been the standout player'

Brassell isn't alone in tipping Kvaratskhelia to win the Ballon d'Or - talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor made a similar case in July.

The former Aston Villa hero insisted the 25-year-old has had a bigger impact than other contenders, insisting World Cup winner Yamal and Kane were less decisive for their respective teams.

Agbonlahor told talkSPORT: "Do you know the player that I would give it to? [Kvicha] Kvaratskhelia.



"But if you think about the best player to watch with your two eyes has been Kvaratskhelia all season for PSG.

5 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia scored 19 goals in all competitions for PSG in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: Getty

"He's been the standout player – more than Lamine Yamal; more than Harry Kane; more than everyone else."

Sports.title: 'If we fail, it won't be Sergej's fault... I'll stand by him': Hull City owner ACUN ILICALI's promise to boss Jakirovic, a recruitment 'disaster' he's desperate to avoid and his masterplan for transfer window 'that will decide Hull's next five years'
Sports.content:
'If we fail, it won't be Sergej's fault... I'll stand by him': Hull City owner ACUN ILICALI's promise to boss Jakirovic, a recruitment 'disaster' he's desperate to avoid and his masterplan for transfer window 'that will decide Hull's next five years'

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The Hull City owner Acun Ilicali is tackling the question ‘Will you be tempted to sack your manager if you are bottom of the Premier League at Christmas?’ when Sergej Jakirovic walks through the room at the club’s training ground where our interview is taking place.

Given that everyone seems to be predicting the club to go straight back down to the Championship, this feels rather awkward.

Ilicali does not generally flinch, however, and as Jakirovic disappears into a side room, from where you suspect our conversation will remain entirely audible, he proceeds to explain why he and his manager are ‘completely matching’ in a way that he and Liam Rosenior, whom he dismissed two summers ago, were not.

So, does he think the Bosnian will be here this time next year? ‘Yes, yes, yes,’ Ilicali insists. ‘Some things happen unexpectedly in life. It’s like that in marriage. Are you always together until death? No. But if there are some failures, it will not be Sergej’s fault. Maybe the players will be young, inexperienced, new to the Premier League.

'Of course, I will stand by him if he loses games. I will not be judging him by the position in the table. It will be what can we do more to make him successful.’

History tells us that it can be hard to sustain that magnanimity in the white heat of the Premier League, where battle will be rejoined this weekend as Hull entertain Manchester United.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali is on typically honest and engaging form when he meets Daily Mail Sport on the eve of the new Premier League season

Ilicali is under no illusions about the scale of the task in front of him. 'The next five years of the club’s history will be decided in the next two months,’ he admits

Ilicali recounts some very good reasons for belief in the 49-year-old Jakirovic, who took the club from the jaws of Championship relegation to the top flight, but the size of the challenge up ahead looks formidable. Ilicali has established a transfer budget, including transfer fees and wages, of £200million, in a break-neck process of squad-building which, he says, will see 15 new players through the door and be era-defining.

‘The next five years of the club’s history will be decided in the next two months,’ he relates. ‘And what we are trying to do is complicated. If you fail, you will be relegated. If you are not careful, you will have players you are then not able to sell. And at worst, this situation can be a disaster for a club.’

In an ideal world, Hull would be able to lure back Liam Delap, the loanee who did so much for the club two years back, but the wages Chelsea would want for sending him back to Humberside would, Ilicali reveals, be double the club’s average. ‘We love him and I hope he loves us but for this season, I didn’t even ask Chelsea.’

With typical candour, Ilicali declares that good players with Premier League pedigree – often cited as a necessity for the newly-promoted – will simply not be keen enough to justify him spending all summer chasing after them.

‘These boys don’t come easily,’ he says. 'A good, experienced, successful player in the Premier League will have four or five options. Why should he choose a team that everybody thinks will be relegated?

'It is easy to say, “Get the Premier League boys and be safe” but most of the boys you can bring from the Premier League will not be wanted by their club, so you will not be able to take the shiny ones. Manchester United or City will take those shiny ones, but they will not come to us.’

Instead, Ilicali and his recruitment team have looked further afield to the leagues of Germany, Italy, France and Spain which he – and there‘s a clear sense that the Turkish entrepreneur and media mogul is driving the thinking here – sees as close enough in quality to justify investment.

‘So instead of Premier League players past the top of their careers, I go for those who have the dream of playing in the Premier League,’ Ilicali says. ‘Boys who want to play in the best league in the world.’

‘Instead of players past the top of their careers, I go for those who have the dream of playing in the Premier League'

Ilicali owns a Rolls Royce with amber trim, and has now bought the property in Ferriby he was previously renting

A hands-on owner, he has spoken personally to every single player Hull have signed this summer

It means the new roster includes Nobel Mendy, a 22-year-old, £20million Senegalese centre back from La Liga’s Rayo Vallecano, Greek keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, 23, from Olympiacos, and Lucas Gourna-Douath, also 23, from Red Bull Salzburg, with Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia in the club’s sights.

Teenage Australia defender Lucas Herrington has arrived from Colorado Rapids. A move for Everton’s Tim Iroegbunam, an excellent midfield ball-winner, is still conceivable despite a hamstring injury which will keep him out for three weeks.

The acquisitions illustrate a desire to spread the risk, prevent salary overload and potentially bring players who will prosper and bring sell-ons, giving Hull more money to reinvest.

As well as the uncertainty about how these players will fare in the white heat of the top flight, assimilating as many as 15 incomers – nine are through Hull’s door and six more are sought – can bring fiendish challenges. But Ilicali is unmoved by the ‘ifs’ and ‘buts’ and adamant that good individuals, rather than proven individuals, are the ones for him.

‘I have to say something very clearly. This team has a family spirit and this brought us to the Premier League,’ he says. ‘We want hungry players, real professionals, dedicated people. I like the word "dedicated" in life. Dedicated people get success. So, "dedicated" is a word in our transfers.’ He’s spoken individually to every player they’ve signed, he says, and will continue doing so until the last one is in.

This is an individual who will certainly never die wondering what might have been. He rose from a job as a TV football reporter to become a multimillionaire reality TV entrepreneur. He sees this challenge as the latest of many.

‘We are ready for every scenario,’ says Ilicali. ‘This is life. Life can bring you anything. What we have to do is to make the correct choices, though make the risk as low as possible, for the future of the club.’

It cannot have helped, we put it to him, that no sooner had the side won promotion, he was parting company with his sporting director, Jared Dublin, whose CV had included time at Sheffield United during their ninth-place Premier League finish in 2020.

Hull's much-changed squad now includes Nobel Mendy, a 22-year-old, £20million Senegalese centre back from La Liga’s Rayo Vallecano

There are high hopes for Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis after his move from Olympiacos

Ilicali says Dublin’s pay expectations after promotion in last May’s play-off win over Middlesbrough simply exceeded what he was willing to stretch to. ‘Jared just valued himself [at a level] which for our principle was not possible,’ he relates. ‘I respect him and wish him success. I respect everybody about their own careers. Football is so dynamic, tomorrow you do not know who will be with you.’

He has replaced the American with his compatriot Okan Ozkan, former assistant sporting director in the bearpit of Fenerbahce, with whom he worked for a year when juggling his media career and Hull ownership with a role overseeing the Turkish side’s football operations. ’It will be zero problem,’ he says of Dublin’s departure. ‘Okan is a very successful boy, who I have worked with in this setting, and he has a very good future. It will be seamless.’

The same booming confidence comes back when we put it to him that some people are projecting Hull to finish bottom of the league. ‘Some?’ he asks. ‘Not just some! Most of the predictions have us there! It’s like last year, when 80 per cent of the football people in England were thinking we were going to be relegated from the Championship.

‘I just hope that one day I am one of the analysts so I can see what this job is like. In Turkish there’s an expression: "Don’t talk from where you are lying." [Yattığın yerden konuşma, literally ‘don’t pontificate from a position of comfort’.] ‘To those who are sceptics, I say: “Come here and see us first.”’

The evidence of the sea-change is visible at the club’s MKM Stadium, a few miles away, where building work to upgrade the club’s media facilities was ongoing in the heat of last Friday.

That lunchtime’s Hull Daily Mail reflected the sense of transformation. The back page lead featured new signing Mendy declaring: ‘I’m ready for the challenge.’ There was further analysis on one of the club’s targets, young Deportiva La Coruna star Yeremay Hernandez, while Herrington told the paper that his Hull move fulfilled a ‘dream’ of Premier League football. New defender Matt Targett declared himself ready to battle for a first-team place and striker Joe Gelhardt’s imminent move from Leeds United was also reported.

So, which promoted Premier League club are Hull modelling themselves on? ‘Leicester City ten years ago!’ Ilicali jokes. ‘That’s the best model of all! But no - I am humble, so I will say Brentford and Brighton – both clubs that have managed to be sustainable and successful in the Premier League.’

His distinctive Rolls Royce with amber Hull City trim is parked up outside and the weekend ahead would be spent overseeing building work on the detached property at rural Ferriby with views across the Humber Estuary which he has now bought, having previously rented it.

Ilicali says he will stand by boss Sergej Jakirovic after he delivered the miracle of promotion from the Championship last year

‘I love to be the “underdog”. And it would be as good as promotion this year to stay in the league'

He has been the only Premier League owner this summer to have offered regular engagement with his club’s fans over transfers on social media. His posting of national flags on Twitter/X, denoting the nationality of players incoming and egg timer icons, signalling work still underway, demonstrated that in so many ways he is not the typical Premier League owner.

‘I was seeing some fake information about some players that we were "interested" in, which was agents using us and giving unnecessary hope to my fans,’ he says. ‘I’ve always had a relationship with the fans of this club, that I think deserve to have transparency.

'When I looked at our new transfer targets, I thought it was like the United Nations! Be proud that so many countries were now associated with our club. I’m someone who once queued for a ticket for games and this boy became the owner of this club, so I like to think that in some small way I’m representing the ordinary fan.’

It may encourage those Hull supporters wondering what on earth this autumn holds that he is already casting an eye to how next summer might be. ‘I love to be the “underdog”, because there’s no translation of this word in Turkish,’ Ilicali reflects.

‘It would be as good as promotion this year to stay in the league. And if we do stay up, people will maybe say: “Hull can fight for the top ten.” So then we can bring in the stars.’

Sports.title: Joe Root's second coming as England captain unpacked: The mistakes he needs to learn from, how he'll throw away the 'comfort blanket' and why his lack of 'main character energy' will help the dressing room
Sports.content:
Whatever concerns England fans may have about the decision to reappoint Joe Root to the captaincy as the Test team embark on yet another of their resets, no one can accuse him of lacking self-awareness.

‘I think the hardest thing for me will be people’s opinion of how I captained four years ago,’ he recently told Sky Cricket’s podcast, as if pre-empting the likely criticism.

As he very well knows, positioning himself as the candidate for change simply isn’t an option. Root has already captained England in more Tests than anyone (65), to more victories (27) and more defeats (27).

He also knows that his best bet – perhaps his only bet – is to leave the past behind: of the 15 men to have done the job for at least 25 Tests, only Graham Gooch, Mike Atherton and David Gower have a worse win/loss ratio.

On one level, Root deserves sympathy, since his first crack at the job was ultimately derailed by the Covid pandemic. Now, on the brink of his second, he will be without Ben Stokes, a handicap that no England captain has had to suffer since the early days of Alastair Cook.

Root does not return in a position of strength. England have won only two of their last ten Tests, and no series since the end of 2024. The situation isn’t quite as dire as when Stokes replaced Root four years ago: back then, they had won one out of 17, giving birth to the briefly liberating effects of Bazball.

Joe Root does not return to the captaincy in a position of strength. England have won only two of their last 10 Tests

The returning captain's approach so far has been to position himself as a steady hand on the tiller

But it’s pretty bad, and Root’s approach so far has been to position himself as a steady hand on the tiller, a been-there-done-that veteran who has learned from his mistakes. Phrases such as ‘I’ve got a wealth of experience’ and ‘I’ve got lots to fall back on’ are not unreasonable ahead of the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, but they will start to grate if we hear them too often.

Quite how his experience can be best put to use is another matter, and a recent dress rehearsal did not bode well. When Root stood in for Stokes against New Zealand at the Oval in June, he allowed a mind-numbing passage of play on the second morning.

The night before, Glenn Phillips – determined to reach stumps unscathed – had swayed repeatedly out of the way of a hostile spell of short-pitched bowling from Jofra Archer. Yet when Root persisted with the short stuff next morning, he ignored Archer until it was too late. New Zealand couldn’t believe their luck, and threw the bat to great effect. By the time England finally took the last three wickets, they had added a rapid 100 and constructed a match-winning 391.

It recalled Root’s decision to bombard India’s tailenders at Lord’s in 2021, when Mohammed Shami was allowed to make an unbeaten 56, the highest score of his Test career, and Jasprit Bumrah, who had failed to get off the mark in 20 of his previous 32 Test innings, made an equally invaluable 34 not out.

The worry, then, is that Root – for all his insistence that he is older and wiser – has not changed much at all. And yet England are in no position to be picky. The Test vice-captain Harry Brook was rendered ineligible because the ECB covered up his set-to with a nightclub bouncer in Wellington before the Ashes, and Root has emerged from the chaotic end to the Bazball era as one of the last remaining adults in the room.

It is to his credit, and testimony to his enduring love of the game, that he sounds very much up for the challenge.

Whisper it, but he may even allow the dressing room some breathing space after the growing tension of Stokes’s reign. There will be no main-character energy from Root, no unwelcome appearances on the front pages rather than the back. What, after all, does it say about England’s overreliance on Stokes that no new alternative has emerged to lead them in the meantime?

In that respect at least, Root can legitimately argue that the Test team is set for a new era, for it will demand others to plug the gaps left by their former captain. Ben Duckett has played 46 Tests now, Brook 38, Jamie Smith 22 and Archer 20. Even the likes of Gus Atkinson (18) and Josh Tongue (12) are ready for more responsibility. The Stokes comfort blanket is no more.

Nor is the midnight curfew, imposed after the Ashes by, among others, Stokes himself, then made to look less than the paper it may or may not have been written on by the Rex Rooms drama after the Lord’s Test against New Zealand.

Root did not use Jofra Archer intelligently during the recent New Zealand Test at the Oval, which England lost

Harry Brook was rendered ineligible to become captain because the ECB covered up his set-to with a nightclub bouncer in Wellington before the Ashes

Root’s decision, made with the incoming head coach Stephen Fleming, to treat the players like adults is an indication of the latitude he intends to give them. In Stokes’s absence, it may also be easier to implement.

None of this means Root is not under pressure, nor that England haven’t risked blunting their greatest weapon. As captain, he averaged 46. In the ranks, that number swells to 53. And since his first spell in charge, he has averaged 54, while converting 16 of his 30 scores of 50-plus into hundreds.

Ideally, England would have allowed a man who turns 36 in December to spend his remaining time as an international cricketer hunting down Sachin Tendulkar’s Test-record 15,921 runs, holding the middle order together without fretting about the captaincy. Root currently has 14,114.

But nothing about English cricket has been ideal for some time now, and while Brook might have been the bolder choice, Root radiates calm – a word rarely associated with the Bazballers. For that, and for his willingness to do the job, English cricket ought to be grateful. Beat Pakistan, and Root may find the power of people’s opinions begins to fade.

Sports.title: Forced hugs, dressing room tirades and the moment the Man City hierarchy began to lose faith: Pep Guardiola bares his soul in new Amazon Prime docuseries, writes JACK GAUGHAN - and it's clear to see why boss knew change was necessary
Sports.content:
Even when signing his final new contract in November 2024, Pep Guardiola knew that change would soon be necessary at Manchester City.

Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak could feel their time together coming to a close during a meeting in Abu Dhabi to decide on an extension amid the worst run of results throughout Guardiola’s gilded career.

The Catalan didn’t feel as if he could leave City in the lurch, that he owed it to them to oversee the start of an overhaul, although had raised the prospect of parting ways so as not to burden the hierarchy, all of whom he counts as friends, with the guilt of wielding the axe if that was their prevailing feelings.

‘At that time, I actually was not sure I was able to convince you,’ Al Mubarak tells Guardiola in the new Prime Video documentary, A Beautiful Obsession, charting the great manager’s final two years as manager.

Convince he did and Guardiola completed another 18 months from that moment. The scale of the rebuild and continued surgery to the squad became even clearer at the Community Shield on Sunday, with Enzo Maresca having a job on his hands to keep the formerly perennial champions competitive on the biggest stages.

Guardiola knew he was not the man to take that on – even if he left with a domestic double and ran Arsenal so close in the title race.

After an inconsolable Kevin De Bruyne – the club’s finest modern-day player – was left breaking down in tears on finding out City were not renewing his contract and the furious row with captain Kyle Walker in the Anfield dressing room, a moment sparking the end of his career at the top, Guardiola’s own shelf life became the prominent theme around City going into last season.

The Catalan realised it was time after a decade in charge, the four-part series revealing the way in which the manager attempted to keep the players on top, why change was ultimately required and how even dynasties can end in fraught circumstances.

Amazon Prime's new docuseries shows why it was clear that Pep Guardiola knew change was necessary at Man City

After Kevin De Bruyne was left in tears, Guardiola's own shelf life at City was in the spotlight

SEPTEMBER 2025

In the weeks before a huge Manchester derby victory – on the back of consecutive defeats against Tottenham and Brighton – Guardiola became obsessed with his players hugging. He had admonished the team down at the Amex Stadium for not celebrating Erling Haaland’s opening goal wildly enough, showing clips of training ground goals greeted with more gusto, and feared for the team’s bond.

‘Look, look at you in training,’ he shouted. ‘Did you do that in Brighton? Look at you celebrating. We are here in this f****** business for that. Do you feel the pressure? F****** hell, that’s what it is about. It’s nice to feel it otherwise we’re in the Maldives, all of us.’

Before they went out to face Manchester United, Guardiola demanded that everyone ‘hug each other for five seconds, so tight’. The instructions were met by bemused faces in the dressing room before being eventually followed.

Guardiola forced his stars to hug each other after being left disappointed by their lack of camaraderie at Brighton

Haaland’s double and Phil Foden’s opener downed United 3-0 but Guardiola wanted more emotion.

‘The win today comes from the hugs before,’ he said. ‘The hugs were not tight. I tried and you didn’t hug me back. I want tighter. Tight and more seconds. I want you to feel my vows to you. I am so proud of you guys and that is the start of what I’m telling you will be great season.’

He showed players the celebrations from the United match on a big screen before they met Napoli a few days later, to continue promoting togetherness and spirit. ‘F*** that is so nice,’ he told them while watching the footage, played to a Bee Gees backing track. Players grinned.

NOVEMBER 2025

Guardiola stalks the Etihad dressing room. He’s made ten changes for a Champions League tie with Bayer Leverkusen, a decision aimed at allowing players who lack minutes to prove a point to him. It backfires spectacularly, Leverkusen winning 2-0. The fortunes of Oscar Bobb, Rico Lewis, Tijjani Reijnders, Savinho and Nico Gonzalez never recover under this manager.

The monologue Guardiola goes on to deliver is a remarkable display and cuts to the heart of his man-management across two decades in coaching.

‘F****** hell guys, everyone has to feel that “I’m going to show them that I’m the best, I’m going to show this f****** b****** manager than the other guys”. It’s a competition between each other and where was the competition today? I feel sad.

‘I feel disappointed in myself for the incredibly stupid things I try to do to make you safe, secure and confident. I feel f****** stupid. I arrived here at eight o’clock in the morning guys. I stayed hours and hours trying to find something to arrive here in your heart. In your heart. And when I don’t get it, it’s frustrating personally.

‘You don’t give back guys. You know what’s going to happen? You will have another manager. When I see one [sad] f****** face at the end of the season, I kill you. When I see your f****** face complaining for something when I make my decisions, I f****** kill you.

Guardiola launched an impassioned rant at his stars following their defeat by Bayer Leverkusen

The City boss' decision to heavily rotate his team backfired spectacularly at the Etihad

‘Work harder, work better, live better. You can lose games and I defend you many times but it’s unacceptable this lack of courage, passion and love and desire to win.

‘When I say hi, you say hi to me. When I hug you, you hug me. I live my life, my divorce… and my family is away for all of you. What do you give back? The f****** performance you have done, all of you. It’s a disgrace, guys.

‘F****** hell, I am really f****** tired. When I see that, I’m exhausted. Drained. I want to quit. I feel alone. When you play like this, I feel alone. Tomorrow you will not see me. Have a lovely two days. I’m going to the media to defend you.’

TWO DAYS AFTER THE LEVERKUSEN DEFEAT

Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano exchange voice notes about the Leverkusen debacle – and for them, the blame lies squarely at the feet of their illustrious manager. It is exceptionally rare for there to be such overt criticism of Guardiola.

Soriano to Al Mubarak: ‘I think our attitude with Pep should not be too negative. It doesn’t work with him. But it shouldn’t be too kind or accommodating either. This is his mistake this time.’

Al Mubarak to Soriano: ‘To pick an entire new team on a game this important is probably one of the lowest points we’ve had. I can’t speak to him, honestly. I didn’t speak to him yesterday. I didn’t message him. I’m so angry. He’s put a mix in this that is just so unnecessary.’

The defeat contributes to City being pitted against Real Madrid and crashing out of Europe before the quarter-finals for a second consecutive season. City have won only one Champions League knockout tie since completing the Treble in 2023.

City chief Khaldoon Al Mubarak expressed disappointment at Guardiola's decision making in the defeat by Leverkusen

MAY 2026

Two days before the final game of the season. Daily Mail Sport has already revealed that Guardiola is leaving in the summer – those who needed to know were officially notified in early April – but he has yet to confirm it to his staff and players.

In an auditorium used thousands of times during his ten years, Guardiola delivers one final video and one final speech. He uses a montage of clips from across the decade with a pre-recorded message over the top, one where he references the poet Tony Walsh and will be shown to supporters after the defeat by Aston Villa that weekend.

He hums nervously as he enters a packed theatre, standing room only. Anybody who is anybody in the building is there. He wants to get the preamble over and done with quickly.

Read the full, untold story of Pep Guardiola's decade at Man City

Part I: The Real Guardiola. From putting 'the fear of God into you' to his astonishing generosity, those who know him best reveal their stories of the ultimate 'football genius' Part II: His troubled first season. Why 'nervous wreck' Guardiola 'set fire' to plans, banished overweight players... and went to war over the grass length, black nets, Yaya Toure, Joe Hart and referees Part III: The journey to the Treble. For the first time, JACK GAUGHAN reveals the secrets of Guardiola's masterplan for immortality - from magnets to Coldplay, a 'trap', a secret weapon and tactical perfection Part IV: Pep and his players. The 'philosophy of crazy' that spat some stars out, took them all 'to a level you didn't know you had', was powered by gravity inversion... and how he slapped down backchat Part V: The Great Reinventor. JACK GAUGHAN reveals the reason Guardiola stayed one more year, how close City came to signing Lionel Messi and the epic parting gift the manager leaves behind

‘Guys, this will be quick,’ he says. ‘Sunday will be my last game as manager of this club. The reason is simple: to go to Selhurst Park, Anfield, League One in the FA Cup - Madrid, Madrid, Madrid - to deal with adorable players that we have, you have to have something that I had – the energy.

‘But deep inside, I know I will not have it anymore.

‘I’m leaving with an incredible gratitude and happiness for all of you. In a few minutes, our fans will know about my departure and before this is released, you deserve to be the first to hear something that I think is better than my words.

‘I need the hugs and kisses. Don’t forget it.’

Guardiola looks like he is darting for the exit before the tape rolls but stands at the back, surveying the scene, his final meaningful act inside the training ground: watching for the human emotion of those around him in a way he has done countless times before.

A Beautiful Obsession launches exclusively on Prime Video in UK & Ireland August 19, 2026

Sports.title: Liverpool unlikely to pursue PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye, Guglielmo Vicario jets in to Turin as Tottenham agree deal with Juventus... and Rodri closes in on four-year Barcelona contract: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Liverpool unlikely to pursue PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye, Guglielmo Vicario jets in to Turin as Tottenham agree deal with Juventus... and Rodri closes in on four-year Barcelona contract: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Al Hilal targeting Chelsea's Pedro Neto - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Liverpool unlikely to pursue PSG's Mbaye

At this stage, Liverpool are unlikely to pursue interest in Paris St Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Talks for the 18-year-old Ivory Coast international have been regarded as little more than exploratory to date.

Talks over a fee for his teammate Barcola, however, remain ongoing.

At this stage, Liverpool are unlikely to pursue interest in Paris St Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye

Badiashile set for Napoli medical

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile will have his medical with Napoli on Tuesday ahead of joining on loan.

The Italians are paying a £2.5m loan fee with an option to buy at £23m.

Fullkrug heading for the exit at West Ham

West Ham striker Niclas Fullkrug is ready to take a pay cut to push through his return to former club Werder Bremen.

The striker has been granted permission to travel to Germany ahead of an initial loan move.

The deal includes an option to buy, and Fullkrug is willing to give up part of his salary to help the move happen.

The 33-year-old, who has a contract with West Ham until 2028, is returning to the club where he started his professional career.

He spent last season loan to AC Milan scoring one goal in 20 games.

He cost West Ham £27m from Dortmund in 2024 and scored three goals.

West Ham anticipate a bid from Aston Villia this week for right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka while Marseille have made an approach to take defender Jean-Clair Todibo on loan.

Liverpool yet to receive approach for Bajcetic

Liverpool have yet to receive an offer or enquiry from Getafe for midfielder Stefan Bajcetic.

The 21-year-old has one year left on contact and spent part of last season on loan at Las Palmas.

Madrid-based Getafe have been credited with interest but are yet to make a move.

Liverpool have put midfielder James McConnell’s proposed loan to Preston North End on hold until the end of the window.

Awoniyi completes move to newly promoted Coventry

Coventry City have completed the £9million signing of Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest.

The Nigeria international was given a send-off at the City Ground during Forest's 2-0 pre-season win over Brest on Sunday.

Awoniyi spent four seasons at Forest, scoring 21 goals in 90 Premier League appearances.

Nottingham Forest paid tribute to Taiwo Awoniyi on Sunday ahead of his move to Coventry

Man United youngster heads for the EFL

Manchester United forward Ethan Ennis is joining Stockport County.

The 21-year-old has agreed a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee with add ons plus a 50percent sell-on and buy-back clause, while United retain matching rights too.

Ennis joined United's academy in 2021 and was in their FA Youth Cup-winning squad the following year, before being promoted to the Under-21s.

He got his first taste of senior football with a loan to Doncaster Rovers, and last season appeared 46 times as part of a temporary switch to Fleetwood Town, scoring six goals and providing eight assists.

He will link up with another former United academy product James Bailey at Edgeley Park, who secured a contract with Jimmy McNulty's side earlier this summer, following the expiry of his deal at United.

Manchester United midfielder Toby Collyer is wanted by West Brom.

Ipswich confirm Enciso and Ouattara deals

Ipswich Town have confirmed the signings of winger Julio Enciso and midfielder Abdoul Ouattara from Strasbourg.

Paraguay international Enciso, 22, and Ivorian Ouattara, 20, have both agreed five-year contracts. The combined fee for both players has the potential to reach £47.3m, with both having played for boss Gary O'Neil in France.

Aston Villa full back set for Rangers loan

Aston Villa have agreed to loan right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic to Rangers with an obligation to buy £3.5m. The Serbian international is set for a medical at Ibrox on Tuesday.

Celtic also interested in Nedeljkovic but Rangers are favourites.

Brighton are keen on Millwall forward Femi Azeez, as Rangers continue to push for Amario Cozier-Dubbery, after their £7.5m bid was rejected on Monday.

Man United to rebuff Fernandes interest

Manchester United have no plans to sell Bruno Fernandes before next month's transfer deadline.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan, are among the clubs who have been weighing up an offer for the United captain.

It is understood Galatasaray are ready to put forward £42.7million for the 31-year-old but his intention has been to stay and see if he can realise his ambition of leading United to a Premier League title challenge.

For more on this story click HERE

Man United will rebuff approaches for Bruno Fernandes amid interest from Galatasaray

It's nearly Hammer time for Piroe

Leeds United have given Joel Piroe permission to travel to West Ham for a medical.

The striker is expected to travel this evening ahead of finalising his move to the Championship club.

With AZ Alkmaar digging in their heels over their valuation of Troy Parrott, the Hammers moved for Piroe on a loan deal, with an obligation to buy.

Joel Piroe is set to say goodbye to Leeds and join West Ham on loan

Ipswich land Ouattara from Strasbourg

Ipswich have confirmed the signing of versatile 20-year-old Abdoul Ouattara, reuniting him with manager Gary O'Neil.

Daily Mail Sport previously reported how the Tractor Boys have been closing in on a deal for Ouattara and team-mate Julio Enciso, 22. The pair worked with O'Neil at Strasbourg last season, before O'Neil left to replace Kieran McKenna at Portman Road.

O'Neil said: 'Abdoul is a talented young player who can play in different positions, so is a very good addition to our squad. We enjoyed working with him in France last season and are delighted to have the opportunity to do so again at Ipswich.'

Canaries making progress on Musaba talks

Norwich City are advancing in talks to sign Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan.

The 25-year-old Dutchman, formerly played for Sheffield Wednesday, is due to arrive tonight ahead of a medical.

Norwich want a winger as Ali Ahmed has injured an anterior cruciate ligament.

City work on Bouaddi deal

Manchester City and Lille working to get a deal for £85m-rated Ayyoub Bouaddi over the line.

As Daily Mail Sport reported over the weekend, Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now.

Lille coach Davide Ancelotti explained why Bouaddi is wanted by Manchester City following Lille’s friendly at Everton, saying: ‘Bouaddi is a very good player. He is available (in terms of his fitness) and he played 45 minutes. But that is only because I have to manage his minutes. Next week we start the season and I consider him as an available player for me.

‘Of course, there are negotiations. There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us! What makes him so special? He has a huge personality.

‘He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18 years old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch. Technically he is really complete. He is also physical, really strong in duels. He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi is 'really complete' according to his Lille boss Davide Ancelotti

Chelsea set Neto price tag

Chelsea want close to £100million if they are to sell Pedro Neto this summer, sources inside the Stamford Bridge club have told Daily Mail Sport.

Neto, 26, has had several interested suitors in this window from the Premier League and beyond. Saudi side Al Hilal have been heavily linked this week.

It is understood no formal bids have yet landed with Chelsea for their Portuguese international, but they are aware of others' appreciation.

For more on this story click HERE

KIERAN GILL

Chelsea want in the region of £100million for Pedro Neto

Rodri set for Barca switch

Rodri has addressed gathered media after landing in Barcelona ahead of finalising his £65.4m move from Man City.

The Spain captain said: 'It's been a few intense days, and I'm thrilled to be here. Playing for Barcelona is a dream. We're going for the Champions League and everything else that comes our way.'

He will have a medical on Tuesday and sign a four year deal.

Former City full-back Joao Cancelo is also due in Barcelona after agreeing to return to the club from Al Hilal.

Rodri arrived in Barcelona on Monday afternoon ahead of completing his move from Man City

Vicario lands in Turin after Spurs strike loan deal

Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has completed his move to Juventus on loan with an option to buy for £8.6m.

The 29-year-old Italian has been on Juve's list for some time and they reverted to him on Sunday after a move for Aston Villa's Emiliano Martinez collapsed.

Villa are signing Zion Suzuki from Parma in a £30m deal. The Japan international is due to undergo his medical today also.

Spurs are pressing ahead with moves for Savinho at Manchester City and their striker Omar Marmoush. Liverpool's Cody Gakpo remains a target too.

Guglielmo Vicario is set for Juventus after an £8.5m deal was struck with Spurs

Sunderland set to confirm Methalie deal

Toulouse left-back Dayann Methalie arrived in the UK on Sunday ahead of his medical at Sunderland.

The France U21 international, a former target for Newcastle, is set to finalise his £25.7million move pending today’s tests.

Dedic in for Toon medical

Benfica right-back Amar Dedic arrived on Tyneside last night ahead of undergoing a medical at Newcastle.

Negotiations are at the final stages with a £29.5million deal in place for the 23-year-old.

The Bosnia international is likely to go straight into the team to play Liverpool next weekend.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering. Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall is one of the names that remains on their radar in the final days of the window.

Nottingham Forest are also expected to make another offer for the Swede.

Badiashile to undergo Napoli medical

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile will have his medical with Napoli on Tuesday ahead of joining on loan.

The Italians are paying a £2.5m loan fee with an option to buy at £23m.

Sports.title: Rodri lands in Barcelona ahead of £65.4m move from Man City and declares 'we're going for everything that comes our way'
Sports.content:
Rodri has addressed gathered media after landing in Barcelona ahead of finalising his £65.4million move from Manchester City.

The Spain captain said: 'I'm happy to be here; it's been a few intense days, and I'm thrilled to be here.

'Playing for Barcelona is a dream. We're going for the Champions League and everything else that comes our way.'

He will have a medical tomorrow ahead of being officially unveiled potentially on Wednesday.

Rodri will sign a four-year contract until 2030, just a month after he captained Spain to World Cup glory. After a seven-year spell with City, he will now return to his homeland.

He agreed to join Barcelona two weeks ago after informing rivals Real Madrid he no longer wished to join them.

Rodri has arrived in Barcelona ahead of signing for the club from Manchester City

The opening offers, however, fell well below City's demands for £68million.

Discussions have been ongoing with Barca now reaching City's valuation.

He flew to Spain on Monday evening and will now progress with the process of officially becoming a Barcelona player.

Rodri returned to Manchester from his break after winning the World Cup on Thursday, taking a Ryanair flight from Madrid to Liverpool but was not involved in today's Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

City now intend to press ahead with their move for Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille but still want another midfielder.

Sports.title: 'I was a young wolf,' admits new boss Sebastien Pocognoli as he promises to bring passion, energy and clear thinking to the Scotland job
Sports.content:
In a previous life, Sebastien Pocognoli was a young firebrand who certainly knew how to light the blue touchpaper back home in Belgium.

Whilst playing for his hometown club Standard Liege, Pocognoli was determined to lap it up after a 6-2 thrashing of their bitter rivals Charleroi back in 2012.

In an incident which carried echoes of Graeme Souness in Turkey, Pocognoli planted a Liege flag in the centre spot after the match and would later be charged and fined by police for inciting violence.

'It was a long time ago,' reflected the 39-year-old, who was unveiled as Scotland's new head coach after signing a two-year deal to replace Steve Clarke.

'I was a young wolf. But actually, it was slightly too much. I will not do that again. Be careful with passion. Too much passion can be also too much and cross the line.

'You need to find the balance - to be analytic and to be passionate. If you just react only with passion, you make mistakes.

Scotland's new head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli, gets a feel for the pitch at Hampden Park

'I am passionate but I also try to be analytical. I am very energetic on the touchline and in my relationship with the players.

'But I also try to be calm in the right moments because I need to make good choices and I need to have a clear head.

'You also need a good staff around you to help to have a good voice and give good advice. Yes, passion is good but you cannot react to everything with fire.'

If Pocognoli can bring success to Scotland and bring a more modern style of play, the Tartan Army will get fully on board with the new Wolf of Mount Florida.

He was calm and measured at Hampden today, speaking alongside SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland, both of whom led the recruitment process.

Pocognoli spoke decent English and expressed his desire to play on the front foot whilst bringing through young players and refreshing the squad.

All of this would have been music to the ears of most Scotland fans. The whole setup had gone flat and stale under Clarke, underlined by Scotland's miserable offering in the World Cup.

Maxwell also spoke today about the need for the country to embrace change, to embrace a more modern approach, and the feeling that Scotland are ready for a new direction.

That is, of course, broadly correct. But there was a slight irony in the fact that the change has almost happened by accident, with Clarke walking away from a four-year deal handed to him prior to the World Cup.

Had that resignation not happened, we wouldn't be in this position. But that's by the by. Pocognoli is the man entrusted with taking Scotland forward and bringing a sense of excitement and ambition to the team.

In terms of his credentials, he had a short stint in charge of Monaco last season. He won 16 of his 38 matches, scored plenty of goals, albeit they conceded quite a few at the other end as well.

The highlight was a 3-1 win away from home over Paris Saint-Germain, part of a home and away double over the European champions. Pocognoli also oversaw victories over Marseille and Lyon.

At USG in Belgium, he won a championship, which was the club's first league title in 90 years. With the SFA tapping into data now more than ever before, he ticked a lot of boxes.

If it's a risky appointment or a gamble, the SFA have rolled the dice and done exactly what many fans have been asking them to do.

'Like many coaches, you say you want to be dominant,' said Pocognoli of his style of play. 'That's the reality.

'But, of course, it is easy to say be dominant on paper and in training tell that to the players, but to make it happen in the heads of the players in games is a big difference.

'I like to defend on the front foot, be high up the pitch. The risk is to give some space at the back but there is more chance to be dangerous high up the pitch.

Pocognoli was appointed after a recruitment process led by Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell

'So yes, to be direct, have good passing options and keep the qualities of Scottish football - be passionate, win more duels than the opponent. That to me is very important.

'Change can be a really aggressive word. It's not like changing the page in a book. It is about trying to continue and trying to improve for the benefit of Scottish football.

'I hope I can be the right man for this two-year contract and I think Craig and Ian really want to help the process to continue to develop Scottish football in terms of structure.

'Also, following the young talent, to work more closely with the clubs and to try to improve things. It's a positive approach and I hope it will be a good fit.'

One of the main criticisms levelled at Clarke over the years was his reluctance to give a chance to young players, that he became too loyal and too reliant on the old guard.

The likes of Findlay Curtis, Lennon Miller and Kieron Bowie now have a manager who seems far more open to blooding young talent.

Indeed, a key part of the remit for Pocognoli is helping bring through the next generation, whilst still delivering results in the here and now.

Robbie Ure is another who should be firmly on his radar, the young striker having just completed a big-money move to Sevilla.

'That is in my baggage - to work with young players,' said the new Scotland boss, whose first matches will come against Slovenia and Switzerland when the Nations League gets under way next month.

'It is easier to do in daily work, because you can help them daily. At the end of my playing career I went straight into an academy at Union SG and Genk and also the national team when you are 18-20 years old.

'I know the routine of the national teams and how players have to get used to that routine.

'In Union it was a project to develop players. That is something I like to do. At Monaco in a short period of time I developed many good players.

'You can see they sold a lot of players this summer and I was only there for six months. That shows what I can do.

'But the national team needs a different approach, you need the clubs, you need to have the support from clubs and I hope I can stimulate this.

'It's to find the right balance between trying to get the right results, otherwise you will be on me! And also to find the opportunity to develop some players.

Pocognoli says it is 'really positive' to see young Scots such as Kieron Bowie playing in Italy

'When you test or try things, it's also a part of risk. You have to accept that I'll try to get the benefit of a result and also develop and be ready for what is coming next season. I want to go through the processes and challenges.

'I think there are some exciting names who will come [into the squad]. It will depend who is progressing at their clubs and what they achieve.

'It is not easy to go at a very young age in Italy [as Miller and Bowie have done] with very specific football culture. But it can only be really positive for Scottish football.

'There are a lot of names to follow. But also I would like to see these young names growing in the top clubs in Scotland because that's where you want to see them. That is something very important for me too, to follow the young talents here.'

The winds of change have blown through Hampden. There is a freshness to all of this. A lot of Scotland fans will be on board with Pocognoli purely because of the fact he's not Steve Clarke.

If the Belgian can deliver a modern, attacking brand of football and impart meaningful change, the Tartan Army could be set for an exciting new chapter.

Sports.title: Man United stand firm on captain Bruno Fernandes' transfer stance as Galatasaray 'prepare stunning DOUBLE-your-money salary offer' and £43m bid for Portugal international
Sports.content:
Manchester United insist Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price this summer.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan, are among the clubs who have been weighing up making an offer for the United captain.

Indeed, it is understood Galatasaray are ready to put forward a £42.7million offer for the 31-year-old plus a substantial increase on his salary.

A £57m release clause in the Portugal international's contract for foreign clubs expired last month and United know it would take considerably more to replace him, especially in the current inflated market.

As yet, no offer has been received, and senior United sources say interested parties would be wasting their time. Daily Mail Sport revealed in March that United were planning to instigate talks over a new deal for Fernandes. As it stands, talks remain at the preliminary stage.

Galatasaray and other suitors believe the lack of a new contract for Fernandes is a weak spot they can exploit.

Manchester United are readying themselves for a £42.7million swoop for their captain Bruno Fernandes from Galatasaray

Fernandes has one year left on his current deal with an option for a further year. He is already one of the best paid players in the club, behind Marcus Rashford, on around £220,000 a week.

The club captain was, however, hurt by the club's stance last year when Al Hilal were prepared to offer £100m for him.

The club said it was up to Fernandes whether he wanted to leave and the Portugal international felt they should have expressed a greater desire to keep him, to underline his importance.

Fernandes went on to achieve a Premier League record 21 assists last season and is favourite to be crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26 in Manchester next week.

Despite the allure of greater riches in Saudi Arabia or elsewhere, his ambition has been to stay at Old Trafford and see if he can realise his ambition of leading United to a Premier League title challenge.

Throught the turmoil of Ruben Amorim's tenure and the revival under Michael Carrick, Fernandes has remained close to each coach and been a model professional leading by example on the pitch.

Fernandes, who will be speaking to an audience of fans at invite-only event at Manchester's Arndale centre on Tuesday, said earlier this summer: 'It's not a question of loyalty. I could have gone two years ago, I could have gone three years ago, I could have gone last season, but I really like to be here.

'I think that being successful at this club is something that I can never get at another club. The joy and everything I get, the day I get what I want from this club, I don't think I will get that from any other club in the world.' He told Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's side, however, insist the 31-year-old is not available for transfer at any price

'I won the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup (but) what this club wants, what these fans want and what I want, myself and the team, we haven't got that yet. Until my contract expires, I'm going to try.'

According to The Telegraph, Dursun Ozbek, the Galatasaray president, is on a mission to sign Fernandes and is prepared to essentially double his money.

The wage on offer is £18.3m annually, which, due to Turkey’s relaxed tax system, means he would take home twice what he earns at United.

The report suggests an offer from Galatasaray would feature an initial bid plus add-ons.

Performance-related add-ons reportedly include £1.3m for every title win up to £5.1m, plus £1.7m if Fernandes is the league’s top assister in his first season or £1.3m if he achieves the accolade in his second.

They could also include £850,000 if Galatasaray qualify for next season’s Champions League, plus another £850,000 if they reach the last-16 and £3m if they reach the quarter-finals.

United are continuing to look for at least one more signing this summer to strengthen Carrick's hand.

They have bid for Leicester City midfielder Louis Page, along with Arsenal, and want a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw.

However, one midfielder who may yet leave is Toby Collyer who has attracted enquiries from West Bromwich Albion. Discussions are at an early stage over a permanent move.

Sports.title: FIFA chief operating officer sacked weeks after accusing president Gianni Infantino of having 'deceived' staff over controversial World Cup sell-off plans
Sports.content:
Kevin Lamour, the FIFA chief operating officer who broke ranks and criticised president Gianni Infantino over his World Cup sell-off plan, has been sacked.

The French-Swiss executive had released an explosive statement declaring that staff had been ‘deceived’ by under-fire Infantino following his now-abandoned proposal, which would have seen stakes in the tournament sold to private investors.

He would now appear to have paid the price.

A FIFA spokesperson said: ‘FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA’s Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026.

‘FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future.

‘No further comment will be made on the matter.’

FIFA confirmed chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, centre, has left, weeks after accusing president Gianni Infantino of having 'deceived' staff over plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

Lamour had declared the plans were a 'project of one person' as he criticisted Infantino, pictured, while acknowledging he was willing to lose his job by speaking out

FIFA'S LETTER TO STAFF Dear FIFA Vice Presidents, dear members of the FIFA Council, I hope you are keeping well. I would like to provide you with an important update regarding a change within the FIFA Administration. Following recent discussions, FIFA and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour have agreed to part ways. This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally. Kevin joined FIFA in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements. You will have seen Kevin present in each FIFA Council meeting since his appointment in 2024, and many of you will have had a regular working relationship with Kevin on projects of various kinds since his joining FIFA. I felt it was important that I personally provide you this update and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of FIFA on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future. I look forward to seeing you again shortly and, of course, remain at your full disposal should you have any questions on this or any other matter. All the very best, Mattias Grafström FIFA Secretary General

Staff were made aware of Lamour’s abrupt departure in an email sent by general secretary Mattias Grafstrom on Tuesday night. It has been claimed to Daily Mail Sport that Grafstrom – rather than Infantino – delivered the bullet to Lamour. FIFA have been contacted for comment on the claim.

In the wake of the sell-off plan being made public, Lamour told the Associated Press ‘It is the project of one person. Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.’

Lamour also said that he was prepared to lose his job over speaking out publicly.

‘If that means I lose my job, then so be it,’ his statement to AP added. ‘I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’

Lamour follows Infantino’s senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro out of the door. He resigned in July citing his opposition to the controversial plans.

Sports.title: Sky and TNT Sports to broadcast player-ref audio during Premier League games
Sports.content:
Sky and TNT Sports to broadcast player-ref audio during Premier League games

Broadcasters were previously only allowed to televise audio between referees and players retrospectively, but the new Premier League season will see clips shown during their live broadcasts

View 2 Images Referees' conversations with players will now be heard (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The Premier League will this season allow conversations between players and referees to be heard during live broadcasts for the first time. Fans will be able to hear audio via the Premier League's domestic TV rights holders, Sky Sports and TNT Sports.

‌



It comes as part of an expansion of the RefCam system. Last season, referees trialled head-mounted cameras which could be used by broadcasters, allowing them to have near-instant replays from their point of view.

‌



Under the terms of the previous agreement, however, the audio captured by the cameras wasn't to be televised during a live broadcast. Instead, clips containing audio would be released several days after the match.

‌



Now, according to The Guardian, the regulations will be relaxed this season and there'll be a limited use of RefCam during live broadcasts. Only one or two incidents from each of the Premier League's 38 match rounds are expected to be shown.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The audio will not be heard live, nor will incidents that are referred to VAR be broadcast due to the laws of the game. In total, the number of televised matches featuring RefCam will increase from 20 to around 45.

Games on the opening weekend of the season won't include the audio experiment, with a trial needing to take place first. The Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref, formerly known as PGMOL, are understood to be lobbying the International Football Association Board (IFAB) to relax existing rules which prevent live audio from being broadcast.

It's hoped that the ability to hear conversations involving referees will help improve the level of understanding between fans and match officials. Former Premier League referee Anthony Taylor spoke last week about the 'intense' pressure and 'constant' scrutiny facing his peers.

‌



Is this a good move by the Premier League? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images RefCam is set to become more prominent this season (Image: Adrian DENNIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Taylor, who retired after this summer's World Cup, told BBC Sport: "Any referee will be lying to you if they said that pressure or that scrutiny did not bother them, because that's a natural human reaction. One of the challenges that referees face at every level is actually understanding the challenges that we face.

Article continues below

"Fear of making mistakes, external opinion, spectators, managers, parents, media, colleagues. All these things feed into creating self-doubt, lacking confidence, and then things can spiral out of control and you lose the ability to actually have any confidence in what you're doing on the field."

Sports.title: 5 transfer options for Jamie Vardy as Leicester legend prepares for final challenge
Sports.content:
5 transfer options for Jamie Vardy as Leicester legend prepares for final challenge

Jamie Vardy is a free agent following his release from Italian side Cremonese, but the 39-year-old isn't short of options for his next club and could make an emotional homecoming

View 5 Images Jamie Vardy is without a club (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

A late-career move abroad followed by a Netflix documentary and his own podcast. It's the kind of sequence that would coincide with a footballer's retirement.

‌



But Jamie Vardy isn't hanging up his boots yet. The former England striker plans to continue playing at the ripe age of 39, with offers on the table from both sides of the Atlantic.

‌



Vardy's 13-year association with Leicester came to an end last summer before he moved to Cremonese in Italy. The veteran scored seven Serie A goals before his contract expired June.

‌



Now it's time for his next chapter - and it could be the last of his remarkable career. With that in mind, here are five options for Vardy as decision time looms.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



1. Sa o Paulo

Headlines were made over the weekend when one of South America's biggest clubs approached Vardy. Brazilian giants Sao Paulo reportedly want the Leicester hero to join their attack, reaching out to gauge his interest.

Vardy is assessing his options and doesn't appear to be in a rush, but Sao Paulo need reinforcements now after going six games without a win. He'd play alongside ex-Premier League stars Lucas Moura and Cedric Soares if he made the move.

Which club should sign Jamie Vardy? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Jamie Vardy scored seven goals for Cremonese in Serie A (Image: Emanuele Comincini/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

2. MLS

If Vardy wants to go abroad again, then perhaps Major League Soccer would be a more appealing move, particularly for his family. With no language barrier, a similar culture and plenty of English stars already across the pond, it could be a perfect fit.

Sky Sports report that at least one American club are keen on Vardy, who already has business interests in the USA. In 2021, he became a co-owner of the Rochester Rhinos, later rebranded as Rochester New York.

‌



View 5 Images Any move will need to suit Jamie Vardy's family (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

3. West Ham

A lot closer to home, West Ham are understood to be interested in Vardy. Nuno Espirito Santo's side are bidding to gain promotion back to the Premier League at the first time of asking and could do with Vardy's know-how.

He was part of the Leicester squad that tore the Championship to shreds in 2024, scoring 18 goals. Vardy could well take the burden off Jarrod Bowen's shoulders.

‌



View 5 Images Jamie Vardy could be blowing bubbles soon (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

4. Sheffield Wednesday

No team is closer to home for Vardy than Sheffield Wednesday, of course, and wouldn't it be a fairytale for him to end his playing days at Hillsborough? Wednesday's new owner, David Storch, has made no secret of his willingness to make an emotional homecoming happen for Vardy, who grew up supporting the Owls and even played in their academy.

Appearing on talkSPORT, Storch confirmed: "Yes, Jamie is somebody that we would like to have in our club. Let's just say he'd be somebody that we would be thrilled to have.

‌



"Unfortunately, we do have these restrictions. We're trying to figure out how to get get around the restrictions to put something in front of Jamie that would make sense for him."

View 5 Images Jamie Vardy is a boyhood Sheffield Wednesday fan (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

5. Rangers

Linked with a move to Ibrox a year ago, could it happen this time around? There have been no concrete reports so far this summer that Rangers are interested in Vardy, but new manager D erek McInnes has just been hit with a hammer blow to his forward line.

‌



Youssef Chermiti has suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury, almost certainly ruling him out of the remainder of the 2026-27 season. Rangers' poor start to the season has the board under pressure to make signings before deadline day, and Vardy might be an option given his free agent status.

If you thought that Leicester would come up on this list, sorry to disappoint. Vardy confirmed on the first episode of his podcast that he wouldn't be returning to the King Power Stadium.
