World.title: Norway wealth fund warns of AI-driven stock market bubble
World.content:
The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

As if the vast scale of artificial intelligence (AI) investments wasn't scary enough, the head of the world's largest sovereign wealth fund is also sounding the alarm.

Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norway's Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG), warned last week that, in an extreme market collapse, a massive loss to its $2.4 trillion (€2.07 trillion) portfolio is "not completely improbable."

The fund, created to invest the Nordic country's vast oil and gas revenues, delivered a record profit of 1,753 billion Norwegian kroner ($186 billion/€161 billion) in the first six months of the year.

Nicolai Tangen, the head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund, has presided over record growth Image: Ole Berg-Rusten/NTB/IMAGO

Yet, Tangen warned that the AI-chip trade — whose lofty valuations helped drive those gains — now poses a serious risk. A sharp correction, he warned, could potentially erase much of the massive wealth built up over the past 30 years.

During what Tangen called an "abnormal" period of low taxes, low inflation and low interest rates, the investments now finance roughly a quarter of the Norwegian government's budget.

Why fund managers remain invested despite AI concerns

While Tangen might sound overly alarmist, Bill Megginson, a leading researcher on sovereign wealth funds, believes many established fund managers share his cautious stance on stock valuations, but are "staying the course, queasily."

"Few managers are inclined to take profits when such a fundamental technology buildout, fueled by literally unprecedented levels of capital spending, shows little evidence of brittleness," Megginson, a finance professor at the University of Oklahoma, told DW.

Major technology companies are expected to invest more than $1 trillion in AI-related infrastructure like chips, data centers and power infrastructure in the race to match or beat human intelligence.

AI is watching you: tracking, traps and surveillance To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

China, meanwhile, is developing capable AI models at a fraction of the cost of their rivals in the United States.

The Bank for International Settlements warned in June that AI "exuberance" risks ending in a bust if returns fall short of expectations.

Why Norway's wealth fund cannot easily hedge risk

Unlike Saudi Arabia or Singapore's sovereign wealth funds, which make large investments in private equity, infrastructure and real estate, Norway largely follows a benchmark-based investment strategy by buying index funds that track major global markets.

Technology accounts for roughly a third of the fund's stock investments.

"The oil fund follows a very passive, broadly diversified global index strategy," Karin Thorburn, research chair in finance at the Norwegian School of Economics, told DW.

Although this approach "eliminates a lot of the uncertainty of picking individual stocks," Thorburn said Norway's GPFG fund managers have "almost no room to deviate from the index or actively hedge."

A strict government mandate means the Norwegian fund cannot take significant protective positions, including holding large amounts of cash.

Most institutional investors, on the other hand, hedge by buying options or futures, which rise in value when regular investments like stocks drop, offsetting some of the declines.

Thorburn, who served on a 2022 Norwegian government panel probing the growing geopolitical risks to the fund, said portfolio managers trust in the collective knowledge of the financial markets.

"If you were to start betting against the markets, you could be right 50% of the time, but also wrong 50% of the time," she said. "So wisely, the government has decided that we don't do that."

How vulnerable is Norway's fund to an AI-driven sell-off?

Javier Capape, a Madrid-based sovereign wealth fund specialist, thinks Norway is "unusually exposed" through its investment strategy of roughly 70% equities and 30% bonds.

"I would not describe Norway as literally 'unhedged,'" Capape said, noting that Norges Bank Investment Management, a unit at the central bank that manages the country's sovereign wealth fund, also uses currency, interest-rate and equity derivatives to protect against a crash.

Norway's strategy also contrasts sharply with that of Berkshire Hathaway, until last year run by one of the world's most successful investors, Warren Buffett.

Berkshire is currently sitting on around $365 billion in cash and short-term Treasuries.

Norway's fund does, however, benefit from continuous inflows of oil and gas revenues from its North Sea fields. In 2026, this is projected to be the equivalent of €63 billion.

Private equity and real estate face risks, too

While its Asian and Middle Eastern peers are more diversified, they face similar risks in their alternative investments.

Some private equity funds have temporarily suspended or limited investor withdrawals due to a severe liquidity squeeze. Commercial real estate has underperformed since the COVID-19 pandemic, especially the office sector.

Capape noted how globally, these alternative investments now account for 24% of sovereign wealth fund portfolios.

Nvidia has partnered with six Wall Street firms to boost spending on AI infrastructure by more than $500 billion Image: Ina Fassbender/AFP/Getty Images

According to the Sovereign Wealth Funds Report 2026, these funds now manage more than $15 trillion in assets worldwide, up from roughly $3-4 trillion during the 2008/09 financial crisis.

They are now "the single most important global source of investment capital for both private equity funds and direct investment in public companies," Megginson said.

How much could an AI-driven market correction cost Norway?

After a sharp pullback in June and July, many AI-related stocks have rebounded, with Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft rising in the double digits in recent weeks.

Some analysts now expect AI stocks to reach new all-time highs by the end of the year. Though what follows is anyone's guess.

"Norges Bank Investment Management itself has stress-tested an AI correction, estimating that such a scenario could reduce the value of the entire fund by around 18%," Capape said.

This would represent around €432 billion being wiped off the fund's value, the equivalent of nearly seven years of Norway's energy revenues.

Edited by: Tim Rooks

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Schools return as new Dutch and maths targets become law
World.content:
Schools in the north of the Netherlands are the first to go back after the summer holidays, and they return to a new set of legally binding targets for what pupils have to learn in Dutch and maths.

The updated core curriculum objectives (kerndoelen) were written into law this month for the first time, NOS reported on Monday. They set out the knowledge and skills pupils are expected to acquire in primary school and the first years of secondary education.

The previous objectives dated from 2006 and were criticised as out of date, vague, and non-committal. There are now fewer of them for Dutch, but what pupils should be able to do is described more concretely. Literature has a clearly defined role, and language development is to be built into other subjects as well.

Junior education minister Judith Tielen said the change was needed because of a serious decline in basic language and maths skills.

Falling standards

The Netherlands was previously seen internationally as one of the leaders in reading, but standards have dropped sharply in recent years.

Tielen wrote to MPs recently that no other European country has seen learning performance fall as far, and school inspectors have found year after year that many children cannot read, write, or do basic maths at the expected level.

Earlier attempts to turn this around – a masterplan on basic skills launched in 2022 and the national programme set up to make up for learning lost during the coronavirus closures – have not had the intended effect, Tielen said. She is working on a new approach prioritising language.

The objectives for the remaining subjects, including two new ones – digital literacy and citizenship – are due to be made law next summer. Schools have until 2031 to incorporate all of them into their teaching.

Ilja Cornelisz, an education researcher at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam, said ambitious objectives do matter because basic skills are under pressure, but that more is needed to improve schooling.

The real task, he said, is giving teachers the professional room, the reliable knowledge, and the support to deliver the goals in their own classrooms, while leaving schools free to decide how they get there.

World.title: Two minors held after second Zaandam explosion in five days
World.content:
Police have arrested two minors on suspicion of involvement in an explosion that blew the back wall off a Zaandam flat in the early hours of Monday.

The blast at the Hof van Zaenden was reported at about 1.40am and was followed by a fire, which the fire service put out quickly. Residents of the block were evacuated because of fears it might collapse, regional broadcaster NH reported.

Nobody was in the flat where the device went off and no one was hurt by the blast, police said.

Officers found the two suspects in a car close to the block shortly after the explosion. Police have not given their ages, saying only that both are under 18.

Debris from the wall was scattered on both sides of the building, and windows and frames in neighbouring flats were damaged. Forensic officers worked with the defence ministry’s bomb disposal unit to secure evidence at the scene.

It is the second explosion in Zaandam in five days. A blast damaged a window at a house on Saenredamstraat late on Thursday, and police are still appealing for witnesses.

World.title: The IamExpat Fair is back in Eindhoven: what’s new this year?
World.content:
The IamExpat Fair returns to Eindhoven on Saturday October 3 for its second outing in the city, with a bigger careers section, two international centres and a new supervised kids area.

The fair, which takes place in the Klokgebouw in Strijp-S, provides advice and services of all kinds for the international community, including special offers only available for attendees. You can register for free online.

“We are bringing back the large career section, expanding the number of expat centres at the fair, and growing the Family & Kids section,” says event manager Claire Leunissen.

Careers and partners

The careers section includes Brainport and recruitment agency Undutchables, and is aimed particularly at the partners of people who have moved to the region for work.

“The international community of Eindhoven can’t be underestimated,” says Claire. “This small but mighty international community also means that we are able to help the partners and families of expats looking to settle into Dutch life as well, through career opportunities, community groups, fitness schools and Dutch classes.”

Families and newcomers

New this year is a kids area, supervised by childcare provider Korein, where families can play while parents work their way round the stands.

Two international centres will be on hand for questions about registration and residency: Holland Expat Center South, based in Eindhoven, and Expat Centre Maastricht Region. Orion Immigration Law returns with a stand double the size of last year’s.

Language schools include Language Institute Regina Coeli in Vught, Una Paloma Blanca, Bart de Pau and Taalkracht, while the health and leisure exhibitors range from bike subscription service Swapfiets to Happy Bodies and Shakti.

Every stage covered

Workshops and presentations by experts run for most of the day, covering renting, buying a house and securing a mortgage, tax, careers and schooling.

“The fair is an incredible one-stop shop for every part of life in the Netherlands,” says Claire. “International students or young professionals might be looking for Dutch language classes or job related information, but a decade later, they can come to the fair and learn more about preparing for retirement, buying their first home, or choosing the right daycare for their kids.”

“We are excited to bring the IamExpat Fair back to the Klokgebouw, a historic building that embodies the history of technology, innovation and immigration of Eindhoven,” says Claire.

The IamExpat Fair Eindhoven takes place in the Klokgebouw, Strijp-S on Saturday October 3 from 10am to 5pm. Entrance is free with online registration.

World.title: Dutch destinations: Move on up to Midden-Groningen
World.content:
The area of countryside known as Midden-Groningen describes itself as the “playground” of the city of the same name. The region is home to country estates, windmills, little museums and plenty of outdoor places to explore by bike, foot and by boat.

Dotted around the countryside you will also see some of the traces of the regional gas industry, which has now been shut down because of the damage caused by earthquakes.

Five things to do in Midden-Groningen

Visit a country house

The Groningen country house, or borg, Fraeylemaborg in Slochteren was lived in by its wealthy owners well into the 20th century, but parts of the complex date back to the 13th. The entire building is now open to the public, from the attic to the kitchens and offers a fascinating glimpse into the lives of wealthy Groningers.

The grounds are also open to explore and regular re-enactments are staged in the grounds. When we visited a medieval battle, complete with tents, villagers and cannon, was being re-created much to the delight of the many children in the audience. The café with its sunny terrace is a good stop for lunch.

Take in a museum

There are plenty of small, regional museums in the region. In Hoogezand you will find the national bus museum, which attracts bus fans from all over the globe, and a historic wharf that has been virtually untouched since 1922.

In Sappemeer is the fire brigade museum and your offspring will be able to help put out a fire on certain days in the summer. Zuidbroek is home to a railway museum, in the old station, with a treasure hunt, train simulator for budding drivers and a collection of model trains.

Check out a windmill

The region is home to several windmills, some of which were used to pump out water when the land was being drained. De Wachter, on the edge of Zuidlaren, is a working oilseed mill with a small museum and great views if you can brave the ladders to reach the top.

It still produces linseed and corn oil, and four types of spices, all of which you can buy in the shop. Open on Saturday and Wednesday afternoon.

Wander in nature

The Drentsche Aa national park, on the edge of Zuidlaren, takes its name from the river Aa which meanders through the countryside from Drenthe into Groningen province. Home to plenty of wildlife and megalithic tombs known as hunebedden, it is one of the oldest landscapes in the country. You can follow various cycling and walking routes and the visitors centre has a welcoming café for lunch or high tea.

See the Veenkoloniën by boat

Pick up a canoe or an electric motorboat at Peddel en zo in Kiel-Windeweer and follow one of several routes along canals and rivers, from one hour to a full day. You will pass through ribbon villages and the remains of old peat workings, with plenty of opportunities to stop for lunch or a swim.

Where to eat

There is plenty of choice throughout the region. De Amshoff in Kiel-Windeweer comes highly recommended for dinner but was fully booked when we were there. It also offers overnight stays. Van Heijningen Bosch in Veendam is housed in a listed country house and serves lunch and evening fine dining.

The Grand Café in Zuidlaren offers traditional Dutch café fare – steaks, spare ribs – as well as cheese fondue and a hearty Dutch stew. Be aware, many places are closed Monday, Tuesday and even Wednesday, so check first.

Where to stay

We stayed in a little wooden cabin in the small-scale complex known as Romala’s Home in Kiel-Windeweer, where they also have a fascinating (enormous) shop full of bric-a-brac.

Het Torentje van Trips is a B&B in a converted water mill which sleeps up to eight in the east of the region. Zuidlaren has a couple of fairly ordinary hotels while Pieks in Noordlaren gets rave reviews online. There are also plenty of campsites if you are looking for something a little less refined.

How to get there

There are some bus and train services, but a car is probably the best, and easiest, way to get around. Rent a bike if you like cycling.

Anything else?

If you are looking for a longer stay, there is plenty more to explore in north eastern Groningen, including the fortified village of Bourtange and lots more borgs (manor houses).

World.title: Warning after Dutch blood donor infected with West Nile virus
World.content:
A case of West Nile virus has been detected in a Dutch blood donor in the first infection of its kind for six years.

The donor, who lives in Utrecht province, is though to have contracted the virus in the Netherlands, as they have not been abroad recently, the public health agency RIVM said.

The virus was confirmed after the patient reported mild symptoms of West Nile fever. Blood bank Sanquin subsequently carried out laboratory tests on a number of samples.

Some 80% of people who contract the virus have no symptoms, but around 1% develop neurological problems, mainly people over 50 with weakened immune systems. In rare cases it can be fatal.

The disease mainly occurs in birds, but can be transmitted to other species, including humans, by mosquitoes. There are no known cases of transmission between humans.

Horse and bird infected

The RIVM said the virus had also been detected in a horse and a bird in different locations in the Netherlands, indicating that mosquitoes that carry the virus are active in the country.

The agency advised people to wear clothes with long sleeves, apply mosquito repellent and use screens or mosquito nets to keep the insects out. It added that the risk of contracting West Nile virus in the Netherlands was small.

World.title: Limburg brewery’s Pils scoops top global award for second time
World.content:

Limburg brewery Alfa has won one of the top prizes at the World Beer Awards for the second time.

The family firm, based in Thull, was awarded the title of World’s Best Classic Pilsener for Edel Pils, which previously won the honour in 2021.

It was one of four Dutch beers to win a Gold award at the annual festival in the English city of Norwich, along with Grolsch’s Cal and Herfstbok and the Gouverneur Superieur Pilsener made by another Limburg brewery, Lindeboom.

Edel Pils was also named as the best Dutch national beer by the international jury.

Alfa has been brewing beer in Thull for 156 years, using traditional family recipes and its own water source.

World.title: Dutch companies to receive €1bn in Trump tariff compensation
World.content:
Dutch companies are set to recoup a €1 billion windfall from the Trump administration after the United States Supreme Court ruled most of his “liberation day” tariffs announced last April were illegal.

Philips, one of the first companies to claim a refund following the ruling in February, received €186 mln, which accounted for around 4% of its turnover for the second quarter of 2026.

The figures were included in the health tech giant’s latest quarterly results, which showed a 4% increase in sales compared to the same period in 2025.

The Supreme Court ordered the US government to compensate companies when it upheld a lower court’s decision that the Trump administration had wrongly used emergency powers to justify the tariffs.

Exactly how much has been paid out is unknown because the government has not published details, but experts have calculated that the top 10 Dutch exporters stand to receive more than €1 bn altogether.

Philips, which makes 40% of its turnover in North America, was one of the first Dutch companies to claim a refund. Other major exporters include Heineken, which is expected to receive between €150 mln and €350 mln, and Ahold Delaize, owner of Albert Heijn, which will get an estimated €100 mln to €300 million.

Altogether more than a quarter of a million companies have claimed refunds worth a total of $129 bn (€111 bn) from the US customs administration, in addition to the $166 bn (€143 bn) which will have to be repaid to American firms.

“We are surprised by how quickly and efficiently this has happened,” Casper Roerade of Dutch entrepreneurs’ association EvoFenedex told AD.nl.

World.title: Far-right FVD-linked school opens in Almere with state funding
World.content:
A primary school linked to the far-right Forum for Democracy (FVD) has opened with state funding in Almere, teaching pupils that “the old Europe was better than the new,” and doing away with the “dogma of equality”.

The “Renaissance School” started with one class of 18 four and five-year-olds. Its founders say the curriculum follows the view of humanity found in classical antiquity, the middle ages and the early modern period.

The school’s site says it approaches scientific views such as climate change as “falsifiable theories” and that boys and girls may be taught differently in recognition of biological differences, NRC reported.

School head Douwe Filz told De Telegraaf that classes are mixed and there are no separate subjects for boys or girls, although material may be presented in different ways.

Pupils are taught Latin and English alongside Dutch, and the school works with printed books, has no wifi and makes limited use of computers.

FVD has presented its Renaissance schools as an answer to what it calls left-wing indoctrination in the classroom, a theme it has pursued since setting up a reporting hotline for pupils in 2019. Ralf Dekker, who led the project for the party, told NOS in 2022 there would be “no woke thinking in the teaching material”.

The school is run by Stichting Tocqueville, formally separate from FVD, although several of its board members and staff are active in the party. Party chairman Thierry Baudet has described it as part of an FVD pillar alongside the party itself.

Questions in parliament

VVD MP Arend Kisteman and D66 MP Ilana Rooderkerk have written parliamentary questions about the school, which will be answered when parliament reconvenes after August 31.

“It is too easy to set up a small school in the Netherlands,” Kisteman told De Telegraaf. “That worsens the teacher shortage and the taxpayer picks up the bill.”

Rooderkerk told the paper she wanted inspectors to step in before four-year-olds were indoctrinated with FVD’s ideas. Judith Tielen, the VVD junior education minister, is drawing up options for tightening the rules and said inspectors would carry out a full quality inspection within the school’s first year.

The Dutch constitution has allowed publicly funded faith and worldview schools since 1917. Most of those founded since a 2020 law relaxed the rules are faith schools, the biggest share of them are Islamic.

Market research tactics

Schools seeking state funding normally have to collect 100 signed declarations from parents, which FVD failed to do.

Instead, the school’s backers used market research to show that the population of the area will increase, boosting the need for a new school.

An earlier attempt to open the Renaissance School in Almere, which was fully funded by parents and private sources, failed and closed in 2024.

World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and whom Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the reintroduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. World.title: Romanian Community to Celebrate Culture and Traditions in Prague
World.content:
The Romanian community in Czechia will come together in Prague on September 6 for the 12th edition of the Romanian Celebration, an annual event highlighting Romanian culture, traditions and the community’s ties with Czech society.

The main event will take place at the Ethnographic Section of the National Museum of the Czech Republic in Kinský Park, Prague 5.

The program will bring together Romanian music, dance, food, literature and activities for children.



Organized by the Association of Romanians in the Czech Republic (ARRC), the event is part of a wider cultural project running from March 1 to November 30, 2026.

Visitors can expect traditional music and dance performances, educational activities for children, cultural exhibitions, book presentations and Romanian gastronomy.

The event is aimed at members of the Romanian community, Romanian-speaking families, children and young people, as well as Czech residents interested in Romanian culture.

According to ARRC, the project aims to preserve and promote Romanian cultural and linguistic identity among Romanians living in the Czech Republic while creating opportunities for greater interaction between the Romanian and Czech communities.

“Through this project, we aim to offer the Romanian community, Romanian speakers, and lovers of the Romanian language a space for meeting, dialogue, and celebration of our cultural values, while also contributing to the consolidation of intercultural relations between Romania and the Czech Republic,” the ARRC leadership said.
